subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Secret Detection in Code
description: A micro-lesson that makes Secret Detection in Code usable.

hook.text: A developer commits an AWS secret key. Within four minutes, crypto miners are running on the account.

buildup.text: Bots scan public repositories continuously, extracting any credentials committed by accident.

discovery.text: Pre-commit hooks and CI scanners detect secrets in code before they reach the repository.

twist.text: Once a secret is committed, it's in the git history forever. Even deleting the file doesn't remove it.

climax.text: A pre-commit hook blocks the push and alerts the developer. The secret never enters version control.

punchline.text: Catch secrets before commit. After commit, they live forever.

quiz.question: Why is deleting a committed secret not enough?
options: It remains in git history forever
